title: Policy modes: observe / shared-disjoint / isolated default
action: Three write-policy modes resolved per session at write-capable entry points (startFeature, cells claim/claim-next): observe (never claims write ownership, unlimited concurrent), shared-disjoint (opt-in via config guards.write_policy: exact-path leases mandatory before write — slice-3 lease machinery enforces), isolated (DEFAULT when the target workspace already has a LIVE write owner other than the caller). Isolated flow: bee OFFERS/creates a feature worktree via createFeatureWorktree and answers with the new workspace path in work language. Condition 6 BINDING: (a) auto-create only with explicit --isolate flag or config guards.auto_isolate=true, else the refusal NAMES the one-liner (surfaced once per session); (b) loud one-line cost disclosure (full worktree copy + where); (c) register/create writes ride the CLI-owned allowlist (guards.mjs:168-175 pattern) — test proves isolation cannot self-deadlock. Regen inside this cell: node scripts/render_plugin_skill_trees.mjs; node skills/bee-hive/scripts/onboard_bee.mjs --repo-root . --apply; node scripts/release_manifest.mjs --write (+ impact_registry --write if suites changed). Canonical source: skills/bee-hive/templates/.

truths: second write session with live owner + no consent: typed refusal naming the --isolate one-liner (red-first)
with --isolate/config: worktree created, workspace registered, caller told the path (test)
observe sessions never blocked by write ownership (test)
shared-disjoint write without exact lease denied, with lease flows (test)
prohibitions: no silent default change for solo single-session repos (byte-identical when alone)
